hook_line: I read the papers backwards, the back page first, where they keep the truth they couldn't fit on the front. Sit on the bass case if you must. Pick a story and I'll tell you what's wrong with it.

opinions.topic: A motorman sees a station that isn't there.
opinions.line: A motorman on the Flushing line swears he passed a station that isn't on any map, lit up, people waiting, and he'd like it known he doesn't drink. Darling, the ones who don't drink are exactly the ones who see things. The rest of us are too busy seeing double to notice anything extra. I've put him in tomorrow's strip, waving at nobody.

choices.label: Do you believe him?
choices.reply: I believe he saw something and the company would rather he hadn't. That's most of what a city is. I'd buy him a drink to hear it properly, if he'd take one.

choices.label: He was probably asleep.
choices.reply: Then it's the best dream on the line. I've ridden that train at two in the morning; I'd stop at a station that wasn't there too, just for the company.

opinions.topic: An assemblyman's tango, not a deposition.
opinions.line: An assemblyman caught doing the tango with the finest ankle in the five boroughs, and the Speaker says a dance is not a deposition. For once they're right. A dance is far more honest. Nobody lies in a tango, darling; there isn't room. If they want to know what a man's like, they should watch him lead. I've seen him. He counts out loud.

choices.label: You've danced with him?
choices.reply: With an assemblyman? I've played for several. They tip in promises, which spend very badly at the grocer's. Stacy makes them pay at the counter first now.

choices.label: It's a scandal, though.
choices.reply: The scandal is that he counts. A man in public life ought to be able to keep time without moving his lips. Write to your representative.

opinions.topic: A sailor named Popeye in the comics.
opinions.line: There's a new man in the Thimble Theatre strip, a sailor called Popeye, all forearms and bad grammar, and the whole bar's in love with him. I draw a penny strip every day for the end of the counter and I've never once made a man that popular. I'm jealous of ink, darling. That's how low the business has brought me.

choices.label: Put a sailor in yours.
choices.reply: I tried. He came out looking like the precinct man in a borrowed hat, and the precinct man bought six copies. So that's a success of a kind.

choices.label: Why is everyone in love with him?
choices.reply: Because he wins without being clever. That's every man's private wish and every woman's private nightmare, and it fits in four panels.

opinions.topic: The judge found at a dance hall.
opinions.line: A judge jails thirty-two girls for dancing in a hall, and a fortnight later he's found in a dance hall himself, keeping very poor time. The Speaker calls it a scandal. I call it research. He wanted to see what he'd been missing. I hope he enjoyed it. I hope the band was good. I hope thirty-two girls were watching from the door.

choices.label: You'd have liked to see that.
choices.reply: I'd have liked to play for it. Something with a long drum break, so he had to keep going in front of everyone. Justice has a tempo, darling.

choices.label: Maybe he was there to inspect it.
choices.reply: Then he inspected it for three hours with a gardenia in his lapel. I've inspected a great many dance halls that way myself.

opinions.topic: Thirteen hours in the air, alone.
opinions.line: A girl of seventeen kept an aeroplane up thirteen hours and sixteen minutes on her own, and the papers wanted to know who kept her supper. Adela put a card in her window about it and the Speaker's own editor came round to argue. I'd have drummed her down. Thirteen hours is a long set, darling. Most bands can't keep time that long without a fight.

choices.label: Would you go up?
choices.reply: Only if they let me bring the snare. I'd keep time for the engine and it would never miss a beat again. Engines are just drummers who don't drink.

choices.label: What did Adela's card say?
choices.reply: That supper wasn't the point. In capitals. It's the best review that girl will ever get, and she'll never see it, which is how good reviews usually go.

opinions.topic: A dance marathon with a band on record.
opinions.line: Sixty-four couples in a dance marathon at Jamaica and the band is a phonograph record. A record. Darling, they've found a way to have music without musicians, and the couples are dancing to it till they drop. Nobody's going to pay a drummer for a marathon again. I'll be replaced by a wax disc and a boy with a crank, and the disc won't ask for supper.

choices.label: Records can't watch the room.
choices.reply: That's my whole defence, and I'll be saying it in the soup line. A record plays the same no matter who's falling over. I play to whoever's still standing.

choices.label: You'd do a marathon?
choices.reply: For money, darling, I'd do most things for a while. But not to a record. I'd want to see the face of whoever was keeping time against me.

opinions.line: Sorrentino and Lusk, ten rounds at Ridgewood Grove, and half the end of the counter has money on it. I don't bet on boxers. I watch their feet. A man's feet tell you he's going down two rounds before his face does. It's the same at a card game, and in a rooming-house hallway when you ask a lodger where the girl went.

choices.label: Who will win?
choices.reply: The one who isn't thinking about his feet. I'll tell you on Sunday which one that was. Predictions are for people who aren't paid to watch.

choices.label: You find people by their feet?
choices.reply: Mostly by their shoes, darling. A man can change his name in an afternoon. Changing his shoes costs money, and he never thinks of it in time.

opinions.line: Five years for a highball, under the new law, and the Speaker says Queens stays on the line for last orders. We serve near beer and cold tea, darling, and Stacy has a house rule for every bottle in the place. If the government wants to arrest the cold tea it can sit at the counter and drink some. The precinct man does, on Thursdays, and finds it very lawful.

choices.label: Is the bar in trouble?
choices.reply: The bar is always in trouble. It's how you know it's a bar. Stacy will invent a rule by Friday and we'll all obey it, and the law will go on pretending.

choices.label: Five years seems harsh.
choices.reply: For a highball? It's an insult to the highball. A good one deserves a medal and a bad one deserves exactly what the law prescribes.

opinions.topic: One note more than the choir sang.
opinions.line: St. Mary's recorded their Easter vigil and played it back, and there's one note on the record that nobody in the choir sang. One note. Low, held, perfectly in tune. The Speaker thinks it's a ghost. I think it's a bass player who wasn't asked and came anyway. We do that. We hear a hole in the music and can't help ourselves.

choices.label: Have you done that?
choices.reply: In church? Never. In other people's songs, darling, constantly. I put a note where it was missing and pretend I didn't. It's the only crime I commit regularly.

choices.label: What if it was a ghost?
choices.reply: Then it's a ghost with very good pitch, and the choir should hire it. Most of the living altos in this borough can't hold a note that long.

opinions.topic: A dog answers the shop telephone.
opinions.line: A hardware store in Woodhaven says its dog answers the telephone, and the Exchange states it's true. I believe it entirely. Judge answers the door at the Harukiya, Stacy's dog, by lying across it. That's the same skill. A dog on the telephone takes the message, darling. It just won't tell you what it was. I've had partners like that.

choices.label: What does the dog say?
choices.reply: The Exchange says it barks twice, which they've decided means 'hold the line'. That's more courtesy than I get from most of the borough.

choices.label: Would Judge answer a telephone?
choices.reply: Judge wouldn't answer the Second Coming if it came between him and the stove. That's what I love about him. A dog with priorities.

opinions.line: Capone gets a year in Philadelphia for carrying a gun, sentenced sixteen hours after he was picked up. The fastest connection in the history of the city of brotherly love. Darling, nobody gets a year in sixteen hours by accident. He wanted to be inside. I'd like to know who he wanted to be inside away from. That's the story, and they'll never print it.

choices.label: You think he planned it?
choices.reply: I think a man that careful doesn't trip over a gun in his own pocket. When a clever man looks stupid, ask what he's hiding from. It's my whole method.

choices.label: Good riddance.
choices.reply: For a year. Then he'll come out rested. The ones worth worrying about are the ones he left minding the shop.

opinions.line: Somebody wrote to the Speaker's operator asking what near beer is near to, and the answer was the 109th Precinct, which has noticed nothing since 1920. Darling, that's the truest thing they've printed all year. Near beer is near to beer the way a photograph is near to a person. You can see the resemblance. You wouldn't want to marry it.

choices.label: What do you drink?
choices.reply: Cold tea, in a cup with a saucer, like a christening. Stacy's rule. I'm told it's very wholesome. It has had a hard life, like the rest of us.

choices.label: The precinct must know.
choices.reply: The precinct knows everything and has decided to know it slowly. It's a kind of manners. I'd thank them if thanking them weren't evidence.

opinions.line: A professor skipped out of his rooms and his landlady's holding his trunk, and the Speaker's sent a man to start with the mattresses. Mattresses. Darling, nobody hides anything in a mattress but money and letters, and a professor has neither. I'd start with the pawnshops and the trunk's lining. A man who leaves his trunk has left something he couldn't carry and couldn't bear to throw away.

choices.label: Would you find him?
choices.reply: For a fee. For his landlady, half the fee. Landladies always know where a man's gone; they just want to be asked nicely and paid for the asking.

choices.label: Maybe he wants to stay lost.
choices.reply: Then I'd find him and not tell. That's a separate fee, darling, and it's higher. Discretion is the most expensive thing on my menu.

opinions.line: Twenty women flying from Santa Monica to Cleveland, and the Speaker's desk attends to their powder. Twenty. I read every piece about them, every morning, back page first. I haven't been sleeping. I've been reading about women who keep going a long way, alone, in bad weather, because they said they would. It helps, darling. Don't ask me how.

choices.label: [Don't ask.]
choices.reply: Thank you. Most people ask. Then I have to be charming about it, and I'm out of charm this month; the bar's had all of it.

choices.label: Who are you rooting for?
choices.reply: The one at the back. There's always one at the back, darling, and she's the one who gets there with her own map.

opinions.line: The Speaker's Pun Derby ends, and a Miss Ianelli takes the final with a horse that came in hoarse. Every week since June somebody I know sent in a card and lost cheerfully, and I used to read them to the end of the counter. I didn't read this one out. I'm keeping the clipping in the piano bench, darling, with the other paper I don't know what to do with.

choices.label: [Say nothing.]
choices.reply: There. That's the right answer. I'll be at the counter Friday, being dreadful. Come and be dreadful back; it's what I need.

choices.label: Was the pun any good?
choices.reply: It was terrible. The judges loved it. Some things you only win by being worse than everybody else, and doing it on purpose.

opinions.topic: A tenant sues over a bedroom record.
opinions.line: A tenant's suing her landlord because the house system kept a record of her bedroom, and the Speaker thinks it's indecent of her to mention it. Darling, the indecent part is the record. I keep a book of initials and the weather and I've never once written down what was said. If walls are going to listen, somebody ought to teach them manners. I'll volunteer.

choices.label: Does your flat listen?
choices.reply: The flue does. It takes my bass all over the house whether I like it or not. That's a different thing. Music wants to be heard; a bedroom doesn't.

choices.label: Will she win?
choices.reply: If the judge has a bedroom, she'll win. If he's the sort who's never been asked a private question, she'll lose. It's always that simple and it's never fair.

opinions.line: Twenty-six women fliers met at Curtiss Field and formed an association, so they can look after each other, since nobody else will. That's what a band is, darling, when it's any good. A few people who agree to keep time for each other in bad weather. I'm short a piano these days. I'd join theirs if they'd have a drummer and a bass that won't stop playing the same eight bars.

choices.label: You'd fly?
choices.reply: I'd keep time on the ground and wave them in. Someone has to be at the end of the field with a lamp. I'm good at being the one still there.

choices.label: Find a piano player.
choices.reply: Juno sits in on Thursdays. She's very good and very kind and she plays it the way it's written. I'm learning to bear that.
